decisions.reason: The target matches and the checks establish a saved toast, a visible title after relaunch, and one database record, but neither the displayed nor persisted rating or temperature was observed; the requested payload and VERIFIED summary do not prove those fields.

The prior receipt contains the required post-relaunch UI rating and independent persisted rating for the exact target, and today's identity check confirms the target and required dependencies remain unchanged, so the evidence can be reused.
On the matching target, the independent database assertion found two records after one submission, contradicting the exactly-one requirement. Required video also failed to finalize and is unreadable.

The matching target shows the requested 4-star sip after full relaunch, and an independent read confirms one persisted record with rating 4. The corrupt video was optional and does not affect this proof.

At the requested XXL text size on the matching target, fresh accessibility and interaction observations show the submit button is occluded and cannot be activated. The default-size observation does not establish reachability at XXL.

On the matching target, publication produced a saved toast, the sip appears after full relaunch with 4 stars and Iced, and an independent database read confirms exactly one sip with rating 4 and temperature iced.

The editor screenshot shows the chosen 4 stars, but the independent post-completion database read returns rating 3 for the submitted record, contradicting the required persisted rating. The VERIFIED summary does not override that value.

The result screen and independent database query support that the sip persisted, but the required continuous transition proof is missing: the finalized video cannot decode from the beginning and fails before the triggering action.
Despite the list showing one row after retry, the independent read finds two persisted records with the same operation ID, violating the no-duplicates requirement.

The requested build and backend are not established at runtime: the installed app serves b41 from r41 and sends requests to dev-A. Passing checks ran on that different target, so they do not prove behavior on b42/dev-B.

On the matching target, the requested display name is visible after full relaunch and independently confirmed in the database. Separately, cleanup timed out and the run-owned fixture remains retained for retry.

The draft was visible before termination, but the runner was interrupted before terminating or relaunching the app, so restoration after force termination was not observed. Cleanup completed; the receipt's success summary covers completed actions only.
